canal_p05_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_001.text: The receiving walk began at the toll counter, where Han's buyer's agent had already spread his inventory list across the public reading board. Luo asked him to move it. He said the list concerned everyone. Tian said it concerned his deposit and Han's loading gear, which was not quite everyone. Yue set the certified pledge extract in the cleared space between them. The agent moved his paper after reading the first heading. Today the canal would begin with its own actual terms.

canal_p05_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_002.text: Pei brought the public receiving schedule in a broad wrapper that smelled of old flour. It had remained in a household cupboard while the toll-house roof leaked, then returned without a new cabinet entry. The ledger's page range matched the archive certificate. Pei admitted she had stopped searching her own storage after assuming the register went elsewhere. The original had not changed overnight. What changed was the question specific enough to lead her to one neglected shelf.

canal_p05_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_003.text: The clerk compared the receiving copy with An Ru's certified extract while Yue read each seasonal total. Sixty, sixty, sixty and sixty completed maintenance days made two hundred forty, accepted under the four annual seasons. Replacement references joined the same totals rather than creating a second set of days. Han listened with his arms folded. He could dispute particular attribution if evidence justified it, but the public copy no longer supported an unfinished collective pledge he could renew through descendants.

canal_p05_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_004.text: Tian asked the clerk to remove every successor obligation from the current notice. He prepared a correction naming the expired labor provision and preserved monetary toll claim. Han agreed after An Ru showed the matching original references. The buyer's agent wrote his own note about failed title value. The canal-bed sale and service lot had lost their documentary basis before any new governance plan was complete. Today's correction would stop the invalid claim from shaping the next week's ordinary bargains.

canal_p05_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_005.text: The agent wanted to take Han's loading gear immediately now that the title failed. His deposit agreement allowed a defined repayment period after formal notification, not a seizure at the reading board. The clerk read that period aloud. Han had until the review term's end to return forty-eight copper or accept the specific security remedy. The agent grimaced and wrote the notice date. Time could be a real contract term, even when a creditor preferred the simpler authority of arriving first.

canal_p05_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_006.text: Bao's private crane test report arrived with the oldest worker carrying it. The repaired support passed the reduced current load, and the smaller swing remained marked. Loading resumed with its ordinary restrictions. The worker asked for the inventory note to preserve that current function rather than price the crane as scrap because the canal sale failed. The agent accepted the measured report. Han looked toward the beam, relieved that something he actually owned could remain useful while something he never owned stopped being offered.

canal_p05_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_007.text: The widow joined the walk wearing a shawl dried on her new rack. She wanted the old neighboring household name, now readable in the receiving schedule. Tian watched Pei trace its number and became very still. It belonged to her father's household in the founding winter, before illness made his own turns possible. The widow's husband had supplied two of those replacement days. A long-resented list had unexpectedly returned a small act of care between two doors.

canal_p05_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_008.text: Tian asked why nobody told her. The widow said she thought Tian's mother had, and her mother might have thought the receipt made it obvious. Pei said the clerk recorded replacement days to protect the seasonal total, not to create a permanent family debt. Tian heard the words but kept looking at her father's name. Yue had no useful reassurance to offer. She stood beside her until the seamstress asked whether they could visit the old house before reading the remaining public corrections.

canal_p05_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_009.text: The old house stood two bends away, rented now by a young couple with a baby. They had no record of Tian's father beyond his name on a lintel board. Tian asked to see the outer doorway, not the family's private rooms. The new residents agreed and moved a basket so she could stand where she remembered a threshold. The place had grown smaller since childhood. Yue watched Tian touch the worn groove in the wood, finding a memory that the official list had never contained.

canal_p05_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_010.text: Tian remembered her father tying a cloth around one hand before carrying a beam. The receiving schedule showed that work in a later recovered season, not the first winter when he was ill. Her memory had joined events that belonged to different years. Pei would help separate the entries if she wanted. Tian shook her head. The legal work could proceed without taking every private memory apart on a doorstep. Yue accepted that boundary and asked what message she wanted brought back to the widow.

canal_p05_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_011.text: They returned to the grain counter before noon. Tian thanked the widow for her husband's two days and offered to help patch the rack cloth after the next wash. The widow said she could take ordinary paid stitching or a simple gift, but would not make the old kindness into a new standing duty. Tian laughed shakily. 'I know,' she said. 'I wanted to choose something after hearing it.' Yue saw gratitude return without becoming the very handle the notice had put on it.

canal_p05_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_012.text: Han listened to the exchange from the shade. He asked Pei whether his mother knew about the replacement turns. The original administrative letter showed she had accepted them. He had remembered the timber price and forgotten the practical mercy beside it. Tian expected him to apologize immediately for the whole successor notice. He apologized for including her current hours in its sale value. The narrower sentence was still difficult enough that the grain counter fell quiet while he finished it.

canal_p05_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_013.text: The buyer's agent asked whether all this family conversation would delay his formal notice. Luo gave him the signed corrected-title finding and let the clerk record its delivery. His business could proceed within its actual terms while households heard their own history. Yue disliked him less after he accepted the two separate tasks. He had an obligation to his buyer, which did not become malicious merely because he lacked the bank's memories. The trouble began when his urgency tried to occupy their whole day.

canal_p05_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_014.text: The next household's receiving entry attributed one season's work to a man who had already died. His daughter said her mother completed the turns and used her husband's old household reference because the clerk's form did not provide a separate field. The total was valid; the person's attribution was wrong. Tian wanted the correction made without losing the completed days. Pei found the offered counterfoil in the woman's needle box. Its signed mark would support a named attribution amendment alongside the unchanged seasonal certificate.

canal_p05_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_015.text: Yue carried the counterfoil's approved copy while the family kept its original. The mother had never asked to become an official public worker; she had asked to have the actual work acknowledged. Her daughter wanted that after hearing the widow's story. Han read the offered entry and agreed it should not be attributed to a dead man's body for convenience. The receiving walk had begun correcting how the bank remembered labor, not merely how it stopped claiming new labor.

canal_p05_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_016.text: A seasonal reed cutter sent his answer through a neighbor. He declined another meeting but offered the outside number of his mother's completed-turn receipt. The clerk compared that number with the receiving schedule without asking for the private letter tucked behind it. The cutter's absence did not prevent a useful correction. Tian made a note to deliver the resulting extract at his actual work camp. She had begun treating a distant answer as participation rather than a failure to fill a convenient chair.

canal_p05_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_017.text: Near the north plot, the household that welcomed Han's proposed sale asked when its blocked drain would finally be cleared. The corrected title had not lowered the winter waterline in its room. Luo explained the access plan beneath the repaired private platform. Bao's new support made it possible to reach the drain without loading the public wall. The work could join the gate crew's next ordinary shift. The household accepted the plan, but refused to congratulate anyone before water actually left its floor.

canal_p05_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_018.text: Han agreed to the temporary drain access under his platform and asked the crew to keep tools out of his dry storage. Bao marked the actual working boundary and a place for contained silt. The access would end after the check, with a separate future-maintenance route recorded. Yue watched the agreement develop from a drawing everybody could point to. Public drainage and private storage could share a bank without one side pretending the other's space had ceased to matter.

canal_p05_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_019.text: The old boatman brought a four-season work token worn smooth on one edge. Its exterior number matched the receiving schedule; its missing weight could not measure missing work. He had been carrying it in a pocket for years. He wanted a new token because the old one looked shamefully small beside the newer successors' papers. Tian offered a legible acknowledgment instead. Pei told him the worn edge showed long keeping, not a lesser contribution. He tucked it away without asking her to turn affection into an official test.

canal_p05_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_020.text: At the third bend, a worker refused to let the clerk describe the old turns as willing service. His father had accepted them because the family needed flood timber and feared being left out. The original pledge's expiry remained valid, but its completed work had not felt generous to everyone who carried it. Han began to defend the founding agreement, then stopped. The clerk recorded the offered account beside the completion, leaving room for burden as well as pride in the bank's history.

canal_p05_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_021.text: Yue asked the worker what the current repair plan should do differently. He wanted paid shifts announced before people were called publicly by family name. Tian had planned to invite households one by one at the next meeting and changed that plan on the spot. The job notice would list tasks and wages, with private replies to the clerk. The new work needed actual people. It did not need the old list's power to make refusal feel like a public confession.

canal_p05_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_022.text: A cargo cart rattled over the upper path while they spoke, shedding one sack at the turn. Grain spilled across the paving near the drain crew's marked work space. The driver wanted everyone to help collect it before the next boat. Yue moved the loose sack out of the walking line while Bao stopped the cart safely. Tian brought a clean cloth from her basket. The clerk kept the receiving papers above the dust, refusing to let a practical interruption bury the newly corrected voices.

canal_p05_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_023.text: The grain belonged to the buyer's store, and his agent insisted spilled kernels could still be put into the original sack. The store worker rejected the dirty portion for food sale and separated the clean recoverable grain. Han backed him despite the agent's impatience. The loss would be entered as handling damage in the private account. Yue thought of the valley's refused dirty cover. She remembered a habit, not a document that could decide today's cargo for its owner.

canal_p05_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_024.text: The spilled sack exposed a tear where a loading hook had scraped its seam. The worker's hook was sound; the sack's reused cloth had weakened around an old patch. Tian offered an ordinary repair after the remaining cargo was moved. The buyer's agent wanted to blame the hookman until the store's own cloth note showed the sack already marked for replacement. Evidence changed his complaint into a material purchase. He looked no kinder afterward, but he stopped demanding money from the wrong hands.

canal_p05_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_025.text: Luo reopened the upper passage after the grain was cleared and the cart's remaining load retied. The receiver walk resumed with dust on everyone's hems. Yue liked the interruption because it had brought their arguments back to things that could fall, tear and be moved. She also knew the paperwork mattered. Without the corrected heading, Tian might still be told that helping pick up private grain was a service owed by the family standing nearest the accident.

canal_p05_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_026.text: The clerk found one receiving-copy line scratched through without a replacement name. Pei remembered a move after the founding winter but not the new address. The seasonal total had been accepted with an associated exterior reference. They could verify the collective discharge without manufacturing that individual name. Tian asked for a public request limited to the reference and season. Someone with the matching receipt could answer later. The missing history would remain a question rather than another reason to impose work on whoever lived there now.

canal_p05_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_027.text: By late afternoon, the walk had returned several completed turns to actual people, identified one attribution correction and preserved a gap. The valid collective completion stayed two hundred forty under the four annual seasons. Han's remaining monetary claim stayed eighty. The grain-house drain had a real access plan. Those facts now carried faces and ordinary consequences. Yue could help finish the household deliveries, inspect the drain access with Bao or compare the final counterfoils with Pei before the evening correction was posted.

canal_p05_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_028.text: Tian asked Yue to walk the remaining messages to actual doors. Bao asked for another observer while he opened the reachable drain edge. Pei wanted help matching the offered work references without letting damaged names swallow valid totals. The clerk would bring all three results to the evening counter. Yue chose the task she could do carefully after a day that had turned an expired duty into family histories too varied for one triumphant sentence.

canal_p05_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_029.text: The last reply list lay beside the new paid-job notice. Yue could carry the bounded correction to households, help examine the ordinary drain or assist Pei with the receiving references. Each offered a different way to finish today's work. The old pledge no longer commanded any of them. The new gate still needed hands, water still needed a path out of one house, and people still wanted their actual parents' work remembered without making their children perform it again.

choices.text: Compare the receiving references with Pei

canal_p05_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_030.text: Tian took the west-bank messages because she knew the doors whose owners disliked officials arriving at supper. Yue carried the east-bank copies in a dry pouch, with the outer references turned inward. At the first house, a woman read the correction twice and asked whether her husband would hear it differently if a cultivator said it aloud. Yue offered to stay while she told him herself. The woman smiled, surprised by an answer that let her remain the person bringing the news.

canal_p05_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_031.text: The husband returned with a basket of pears too soft for the market. He expected a fresh call for work and set the basket down angrily before hearing the heading. His wife's grandfather had completed the last seasonal turns. His own absence from this week's meeting had not restored them. He sat on the doorstep and ate a pear while she finished reading. Yue accepted one for the road after they offered it, grateful for a sweetness that required no interpretation.

canal_p05_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_032.text: At the next door, three children had made a small canal in the dust and were arguing over a crooked twig gate. Their grandmother wanted her acknowledgment tucked inside the cookery book rather than hung on a wall. She said paper near the hearth survived because somebody used it every day. Yue copied the exterior reference on the agreed blank leaf. One child asked whether the real gate would open tomorrow. 'They are still making the timber fit,' Yue said. The child went back to shaping his twig.

canal_p05_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_033.text: The reed cutter's camp lay beyond the last house, where bundles leaned like sleeping people against a low frame. His neighbor had carried a valid reference; the receiving entry matched it. He thanked Yue for coming and continued trimming without stopping the whole camp. He wanted the acknowledgment held at the counter until his next market visit. The camp had nowhere dry enough today. Yue recorded that preference and left with a reed offcut offered for tying the papers, useful precisely because it was so ordinary.

canal_p05_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_034.text: A boatman on the return path asked whether the canal could still hire his daughter now that the household pledge was gone. She wanted paid rope work, but he had feared that signing would trap her into the old family list. Yue showed him the task notice with its stated shifts and separate replies. His daughter appeared from behind the hanging nets and asked why he was discussing her work without her. He handed over the notice, embarrassed. She took it and asked about the actual rope sizes.

canal_p05_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_035.text: Yue knew the ordinary lead line but not the gate crew's final rated hauling arrangement. She gave the daughter Bao's appointment time rather than inventing a qualification she could offer herself. The young woman said she would come if the work matched her experience. Her father worried aloud about wet weather. She said she worried too, which was why she wanted to see the gear. Yue remembered how often adults had mistaken concern for a right to answer before she could.

canal_p05_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_036.text: At a crowded lane, a messenger boy slipped while reaching for one of the correction copies. The pouch caught on a protruding nail and tore at the corner. Yue held the dry sheets clear while the boy steadied himself on the wall. No paper went into the gutter, but her carefully patched pouch would need another seam. He offered to replace it with money he did not have. She asked him to show the householder the nail. Fixing the hazard would be more useful than transferring his embarrassment.

canal_p05_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_037.text: The householder came with a small hammer and drove the loose nail flush. She accepted her copied acknowledgment with muddy fingers carefully kept on its wrapper. The boy helped retie Yue's pouch using the reed cutter's offcut. A clumsy handover had become three modest repairs rather than one heroic rescue. Yue could have laughed about it at the counter, but decided the boy's name did not belong in an evening story merely because the incident happened while she carried public papers.

canal_p05_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_038.text: At the final house, an old man wanted the acknowledgment read slowly because he could no longer see its lines. His son began explaining the pledge's injustice in a louder voice. The old man stopped him and asked for the actual heading. After Yue read it, he said he remembered the fourth season's cold rain. He did not want the account to pretend the work had been easy. She wrote his offered sentence beneath the family's copy, where it could accompany the completion rather than dispute it.

canal_p05_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_039.text: Yue returned with a torn pouch, two remaining pears and the reed cutter's chosen collection arrangement. Tian reported that one household wanted a correction read at its usual courtyard meal, while another preferred no public reading. They gave those requests to the clerk instead of treating every unopened door as a rejection. The delivery walk had produced no new legal finding. It had changed how the finding would reach people, and Yue felt the difference in the smaller stack still awaiting its proper moment.

canal_p05_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_040.text: Bao led Yue beneath the platform after Han's stores were moved back from the agreed edge. The work space smelled of old river mud and the sharp resin of the repaired bearer. They could see the drain's mouth from the dry paving without crawling inside. Its low flap stood crooked against a lodged willow branch. Yue wanted to pull the branch immediately. Bao pointed to the silt packed behind it and asked where that weight would go when the obstruction released.

canal_p05_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_041.text: They checked the house outlet first. The resident placed a basin beneath the lowest seam and showed yesterday's damp line on the wall. Water stood shallow in the outdoor channel; the room's floor was dry this afternoon. Bao closed the upstream small feeder at Luo's instruction, then marked a drain-clearing sequence for the paid gate shift. Today's inspection would remove only a loose outer twig they could reach without disturbing the packed face. The difference disappointed Yue until she saw the heavy mud swelling behind it.

canal_p05_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_042.text: The resident offered a long kitchen poker for reaching deeper. Bao declined it as a hauling tool, but accepted it for pointing out the hidden flap edge from their dry position. Its curved tip revealed a rusted hinge beneath the branch. The gate crew would bring a proper hook, shallow containment tray and replacement hinge pin. Han watched from his stores, worried about the mud against his goods. Yue showed him the silt area already marked on the paving, where an ordinary cover would keep the mess local.

canal_p05_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_043.text: A small crab crawled out of the reachable outer twigs, carrying a scrap of blue thread on one claw. Yue caught it in an empty cup and walked it to the canal margin before anybody mistook it for a sign. Bao said the crab understood drainage better than the people who had blocked its door. The resident said it had also stayed rent-free under Han's platform. Even Han laughed at that, though he insisted that the clause would not be added to tomorrow's access agreement.

canal_p05_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_044.text: The flap's crookedness came from a missing hinge pin, not the willow branch alone. Bao traced the wear at the surviving lug and compared it with the platform's old repair note. A former store alteration had changed the reachable maintenance space, making the pin difficult to replace. Han's father had allowed the alteration. The record did not say he knew it would cause this failure. Han agreed to restore a narrow access hatch so the next inspection would not require another negotiation beneath his loaded shelves.

canal_p05_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_045.text: The resident wanted Han to pay for every damp winter in her house. He said the drain had served before his alterations and blamed neglected public checks. Bao's evidence supported a current obstruction, a worn part and lost access, not a price for all remembered damage. Yue suggested recording the actual damp-line dates and any surviving bills for a separate claim. The resident disliked another form, but she kept the wall marks. Their disagreement remained real even after everyone wanted the drain cleared.

canal_p05_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_046.text: A child arrived carrying a dry rag because she thought adults inspecting water must need one. Her mother told her to wait outside the marked work space. Yue used the rag to wipe the measuring stick and thanked her from the safe side. Bao showed the child how the crooked flap could hold water back even when the canal was low. She listened carefully, then asked why nobody had put the stick here last winter. Nobody gave her a satisfying answer. That failure belonged in the new inspection plan.

canal_p05_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_047.text: Han proposed lending a cover board from his stores, provided it returned without nails driven through its good face. Bao checked its strength for shielding the silt tray and accepted a plain tied fixing instead. The resident asked why so much care could be taken for a board when her room had stayed damp. Han had no defense ready. He offered to help move her heavy shelf away from the affected wall after the drain cleared. She said she would decide when the water actually fell.

canal_p05_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_048.text: Yue made a drawing of the branch, flap and missing pin, leaving the untested length of buried pipe blank. Bao corrected the slope she had imagined from the surface path. Her picture had made the drainage look easier than its visible evidence allowed. She redrew it and added the point where the clearing crew would stop if water failed to leave. A useful plan needed room for discovering another blockage. The resident kept a copy so a future explanation could be compared with what they actually promised today.

canal_p05_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_049.text: At the evening counter, Bao submitted the inspection with its current water marks and agreed access hatch. The clerk paired it with the scheduled gate shift, including the ordinary tools already within the repair allocation. Yue brought the resident's conditional request about moving her shelf. It would remain her choice after the result. The drain had become a specific job with a possible further fault, not a convenient symbol of a dispute solved by finding an old heading. Yue hoped it would be the simpler blockage.

canal_p05_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_050.text: Pei spread the offered counterfoils on a fresh cloth in the quieter room behind the counter. The flour smell of her wrapper had faded beneath the smell of candle smoke. Yue read the exterior references while Pei traced the broad columns with a smooth bone rule. One family name appeared in two seasons with a changed first stroke. Pei recognized a clerk's hurried hand but asked Yue to compare the associated household number before accepting her memory. Familiar writing could still mislead a tired eye.

canal_p05_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_051.text: The two names shared the correct number, and the receiving entries showed the expected completed turns in separate annual seasons. Yue put their copies beside each other rather than replacing one spelling with the other. Pei said the family had changed the written form after a marriage, then recalled a different marriage in the neighboring lane. She laughed at herself and crossed out the memory note. They could leave the variation visible without making a small uncertainty into another invented household.

canal_p05_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_052.text: The scratched-through receiving line had a clearer exterior reference than its name. Yue found that reference in the seasonal index, where the accepted days remained included. Its counterfoil was not among today's offers. Pei drafted the narrow request for that reference and season, keeping the missing name out of the announcement. Yue asked why not print the fragment they could read. Pei said the wrong guess might attach a burdened story to a family that had never carried it. Yue left the space empty.

canal_p05_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_053.text: A young store worker brought the dead woman's daughter back with an approved copy of the needle-box counterfoil. The offered mark matched the exterior reference and the date of completed turns. The clerk could amend personal attribution while preserving the seasonal total. Pei asked the daughter how she wanted her mother's name spelled. The answer differed from the household book's shorthand. Yue wrote the fuller form carefully, suddenly aware that neat administration could erase someone even while paying unusual attention to her labor.

canal_p05_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_054.text: The daughter read the finished name and cried so abruptly that Yue put down the pen. She said her mother had always laughed about the clerk making her dead husband work again, but the joke wore thin after enough years. Pei held the copy flat while the ink dried. No one offered an official sentence to comfort her. When she was ready, she asked for an extra copy for her brother across the ridge. The additional sheet became a small task that Yue could actually complete.

canal_p05_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_055.text: The final counterfoil had a dark circular mark across its day column. Yue thought a cup had spilled there. Pei turned it toward the side light and found the trace of an old seal partly over the stain. They compared the receiving page rather than trying to read the damaged number by hope. The original seasonal certificate and surviving reference supported the accepted entry, but today's counterfoil alone did not recover its whole notation. The difference went into the comparison note. The owner could keep the damaged paper without losing the completion already certified.

canal_p05_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_056.text: Pei asked Yue to read the new job notice aloud before they returned to the counter. The wages and ordinary shifts were clear; the line about replies still said households should appoint workers. Yue changed it to invite actual applicants for listed tasks. A household could help somebody choose, but it was not the employer of every adult inside its door. Pei approved the change and said she would have resisted that wording twenty years ago. Yue asked why. 'I mistook a tidy list for a quiet bank,' Pei said.

canal_p05_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_057.text: The room grew cold while they worked. Pei's fingers stiffened, and Yue reached for the coal pan before asking whether she wanted the window shut. Pei preferred a shawl because the lamp smoke bothered her eyes. Yue brought it from the peg and was reminded that assistance worked better after hearing the actual difficulty. The papers had not demanded a grand gesture. Neither had the person trying to read them. They finished the offered references with the window open and the old clerk wrapped in green wool.

canal_p05_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_058.text: At the counter, Han checked the amended attribution and signed his acknowledgment of the unchanged collective total. He asked Pei whether the missing name could reopen the entire pledge. She showed him the accepted seasonal certificate and its surviving exterior reference. The name request would improve the history, not undo completed work. Han nodded slowly. Yue thought he had begun accepting that a record could remain unfinished in one detail without returning everyone to the creditor's preferred beginning.

canal_p05_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_059.text: Yue and Pei brought the completed comparisons into the evening light. The clerk now had the corrected personal name, the spelling variation left visible and the narrow request for a missing counterfoil. Tian took the extra family copy for the ridge messenger. Pei rested her eyes while Yue read the posting draft. It contained enough certainty to release the old claim and enough open space for the bank's unfinished memory. The room beyond the counter smelled of supper, and nobody wanted to lose that hour to another speech.

canal_p05_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_060.text: The clerk assembled the receiving walk's results after the last cargo cart passed. Household delivery preferences sat beside the attribution correction and Bao's drain inspection. The delivery walker had brought two soft pears from an east-bank doorstep. Some messages would be collected later; one would be read at a courtyard meal. The paid gate crew would clear the reachable obstruction during its ordinary shift and test whether water actually left the house. Yue stood back while the clerk posted the corrected notice. Tomorrow's bank would have tasks to finish.

canal_p05_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_061.text: Han removed the old service lot from his sale list in front of the buyer's agent. The agent struck through its price and added the formal failed-title notice date. He still held the deposit claim secured by specified private gear, and he said so plainly. Han did not ask the households to fill that private gap. Luo watched both men sign the amended schedule, then took down the public-bed offer as well. The remaining private inventory looked smaller, but its words finally matched objects Han could point to.

canal_p05_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_062.text: A household supporter of the sale read the new list and said the bank had made a fine mess of its chance at quick money. Tian started to answer that the chance was never real. The woman asked whether Tian had ever had to choose between winter rent and a slow committee. Yue interrupted only to offer tomorrow's drain-test time. It was a practical answer to one immediate need, and still far less than the woman wanted. Tian followed her outside, chastened by the difference.

canal_p05_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_063.text: The woman showed Tian the seam where last winter's water had lifted a board. She had heard enough statements of principle to know which ones would not dry a room. Tian asked permission to bring cloth covers while the shelf was moved after the test. The woman said she could bring them if she came as herself, not as the bank's ambassador. Tian agreed. Her first useful conversation with an opponent ended with an ordinary appointment rather than a request to admit defeat.

canal_p05_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_064.text: Luo closed the counter before the lamp's oil ran low. Pei took home the public receiving schedule in its new assigned wrapper, with the cabinet return entered properly this time. The original archive material stayed at the valley archive. Tian brought the needle-box copy to its owner and left the ridge copy with the chosen messenger. Yue stacked the dry inspection boards, then gave Tian her old pouch with its weakened seam. Nothing important had to be invented to make the evening feel complete.

canal_p05_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_065.text: On the tenth morning, Bao measured the gate leaf at low water. Its inner edge had swollen beyond the old wear line, and the keeper's repair record showed how often people had shaved it back. Another shave would thin the timber beside a fastening. He wanted the old leaf lifted, inspected on dry supports and fitted with a new sealing strip. Luo disliked taking a useful gate out of service before weather changed. She disliked even more the sound it made when it stopped halfway.

canal_p05_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_066.text: Jiang arrived with the prepared control frame wrapped against dust. She had worked on a local cart brake during the trip and was in no mood to hear someone call every old hinge a spiritual problem. Yue showed her the gate drawing and asked where a small command could help. She pointed to the release selector on the rated hauling apparatus. The stone supply would power the actuator; people would still control the supported load and keep clear of its path. The canal water itself would remain outside the frame's job.

canal_p05_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_067.text: Bao described the temporary plank stop that would hold the feeder closed while the gate leaf was serviced. Its supports and ordinary leakage check needed completion before lifting began. Jiang checked the hauling apparatus rating against Bao's measured leaf estimate, then required an actual balance check on its dry support. Yue liked her confidence less when it slowed the job she wanted to prove herself in. She noticed her expression. 'We are asking wood to behave,' she said. 'It has not read our encouraging report.'

canal_p05_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_068.text: Tian brought the new task notice with two applicants already interested in rope work. Bao arranged separate practical checks for them and showed the stopping calls. The listed ordinary shifts stayed within the twenty-eight worker-days budgeted for repair, including inspection and clean-up. Nobody gained a place through an ancestor's token. One applicant had useful cargo experience; the other had never handled a loaded line and accepted a lighter preparation task instead. Tian watched them choose without calling the second a lesser contribution.

canal_p05_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_069.text: Han wanted the gate work finished before his largest customer's delayed shipment. Bao gave him the working interval and advised an ordinary upstream unloading option if the delay mattered more than the toll difference. Han called it an expensive inconvenience. Luo agreed, then asked whether he preferred an untested gate leaf over a tested landing transfer. He took the upstream option after checking its price. The private cost annoyed him enough to make his agreement credible. He was accepting a limit that had stopped helping his immediate plans.

canal_p05_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_070.text: Pei read the amended work notice to a woman who had never believed the old pledge was finished. The woman listened and asked whether she could apply for one cleaning shift without reopening anything. Pei showed the separate wage line. The woman wanted the afternoon after her sister's visit and no other turn. The reply went into the applicant list as offered. Yue watched the old clerk write a small availability note where she once would have copied a whole household's standing name.

canal_p05_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_071.text: The canal's lower towboat arrived with a letter from the down-fork gardens. Its writer had heard that the old spill hollow would be reopened and wanted to know whether new water would cross planted beds. Luo had sent only a request to inspect, but rumor had supplied a finished decision. Yue read the letter twice. The original charter protected a diversion use; it did not answer where present water would travel after a ridge slide. Their first field trial could not run until the downstream people had an actual say in its route.

canal_p05_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_072.text: Bao added the downstream inspection before the planned trial while keeping the current gate repair moving. They could make a safer leaf without directing a new flood into gardens they had not seen. An Ru would return for the toll-share hearing on the sixteenth day, giving the bank time to gather current operating facts and downstream measurements. Yue wrote the garden correspondent a real proposed visit, with two possible days and no promise that the old map settled the present bank.

canal_p05_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_073.text: That afternoon, the private customer sent Han an acknowledgment of eight copper still owed for delivered goods. The money had not arrived. Han showed it to the agent as a receivable that might help return the deposit, and the agent asked for payment rather than optimism. Yue overheard only because the men argued beside the counter. The future private settlement had a beginning now, but not its cash. Han folded the acknowledgment carefully and went to check whether the boat carrying payment had actually been booked.

canal_p05_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_074.text: The ordinary job applicants returned after their practical checks. Bao chose a hauling partner familiar with steady line work and recorded a preparation shift for the newer worker. Their agreed days would come from the tow crew's three ordinary shifts, not from extra invisible workers. Jiang checked the release selector's movement without loading the frame, using its hand control. Yue wanted to try the command route immediately. She asked her to finish the dry support markings first. She took the chalk, annoyed but aware that the markings were still absent.

canal_p05_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_075.text: Near dusk, Luo found the goose standing in the temporary feeder channel as if appointed to inspect it. She lured it away with a handful of cracked grain from her own feed tin. Tian asked whether the goose needed to apply for a shift too. Luo said it had failed every practical check by wandering under the work line. Bao added a small fence at the open edge before night. Humor had found a place beside the precautions, and Yue did not have to choose between enjoying it and noticing the gap.

canal_p05_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_076.text: Yue spent the evening sharpening the small scraper Bao assigned her for the old sealing strip. Its edge looked unimpressive beside the release frame. Jiang sat nearby cleaning dust from the selector contacts. She said a badly prepared strip could undo a perfect command. Yue asked whether she had ever wanted people to notice the clever part first. She smiled without looking up. 'Every year,' she said. 'Then the simple part breaks, and everybody notices that.' She kept sharpening until the scraper's curl came off clean.

canal_p05_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_077.text: Tian came to the flour-store room with the newly patched pouch. She had strengthened its side and corner while changing the seam's angle, and it lay flat on Yue's knee. Yue offered ordinary stitching pay. Tian accepted because she had given the afternoon to a stranger's rack and needed the evening work to support her own rent. They ate the doorstep pears together, cutting away the softest bruises. Tian said her father had been terrible at threading needles. The memory did not need a receiving reference.

canal_p05_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p05_078.text: Before sleep, Yue wrote the day's two unanswered questions on a small sheet: whether the buried drain ran clear beyond its mouth, and where the current spill water would reach below the ridge slide. Both had visible tests planned. Neither would answer itself because the old pledge had expired. She tucked the sheet beside the gate drawing and listened to the low canal against the landing posts. On the eleventh morning, they would lift a gate that had served too long by being shaved smaller.
